property_summary: After play() is called twice consecutively by the same sender with the same value, pot should be the value of the last call if the first call's random result was not 0 (i.e., no payout happened), but the mutant resets pot to 0 and loses the accumulated value.

After a single call to play() by any caller, the contract's pot should be either 0 (if the random result was 0 and payout occurred) or increased by 10 (if random result was 1 and no payout occurred), but the mutant always sets pot to 0 first, causing the post-call pot to be 0 when random is 1 instead of being increased by 10.
After play(), pot equals 0 or equals msg.value - FEE_AMOUNT (including overflow case) times the number of winning calls
After play(), pot never exceeds TICKET_AMOUNT (10) minus FEE_AMOUNT (1), unless pot equals 0.
After calling play() with exact TICKET_AMOUNT, the pot either becomes 0 (if random == 0) or equals the initial pot plus TICKET_AMOUNT (if random == 1).
After play() returns, pot is always 0 if the caller sent exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, else unchanged
After play() returns, pot is always either 0 or (pot + TICKET_AMOUNT) depending on the random outcome, but never stays unchanged when the caller sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT.

When play() is called with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the pot increases by at least TICKET_AMOUNT before any possible payout, i.e., pot after play() is either 0 (win) or >= TICKET_AMOUNT (no win) but never stays unchanged.
After any call to play() with msg.value equal to TICKET_AMOUNT, the pot always changes (it is not equal to its value before the call).
After a call to play(), pot is always zero if random == 0, otherwise pot equals the total ticket amount paid.
After any call to play(), the pot either remains at the caller's message value or becomes zero.
After a call to play() that does not revert, the pot is reset to zero if the caller's address equals the bank's address.
After a call to play() that does not revert, the pot is either zero or equal to multiple of ticket amount (10) minus fee (1) times the number of wins.
After a losing call to play(), the pot is not incremented by the ticket amount.
After a single play() call, if the transaction does not revert, bank's balance is always 0 (the fee is never sent to bank) in the reference but may become 1 in the mutant.

After play() is called, the caller's balance either increases by pot - 1 (if random == 0) or stays the same (if random == 1), so the caller's balance change modulo TICKET_AMOUNT is always (pot - 1) % TICKET_AMOUNT when random == 0 and 0 otherwise; equivalently, the caller's balance change is never exactly pot when random == 0.
After play() is called by a non-bank user, the bank's balance change is always 0 in the reference but may be 1 in the mutant.
After a call to play() by a non-bank address, the caller always receives exactly TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT (9) ether if the transaction does not revert, never receiving 0 or TICKET_AMOUNT.
After a play() call, the caller's balance change modulo (TICKET_AMOUNT) equals (pot - FEE_AMOUNT) % TICKET_AMOUNT if the caller wins (random == 0), and 0 otherwise.
After a call to play(), the pot is zero if the transaction sender receives less than the full pot amount
After a call to play(), the pot is always 0.
After a call to play(), the bank's balance increases only by multiples of 1 wei, specifically the fee when random == 0.
After a call to play(), the pot either stays the same (if no win) or becomes zero (if win).
After a call to play(), the bank's balance increases by exactly the fee amount (1 wei) if and only if the pot becomes zero; otherwise, the bank's balance remains unchanged.
The contract balance is never reduced by a play() call that reverts.
After a successful play() call, the pot is either zero or unchanged (i.e., not increased beyond the sent value).
A play() call that reverts does not change the contract's balance.
After any play() call that does not revert, the contract balance is exactly the sum of all previous successful play() msg.value minus the fee part that was transferred to bank when the game was won.
After a play() call, the pot is always set to 0 when the caller wins, and otherwise remains unchanged, regardless of the amount sent.
When the player wins (random == 0), the bank's balance should increase by the fee amount.
The pot should be zero after a winning play.
The total balance of the contract should decrease by exactly the fee amount when a player wins (random == 0).
After a winning play (random == 0), the sum of the bank's and the caller's ether balances increases by exactly the ticket amount minus the fee.
When a player wins (random == 0), the bank's balance increases by exactly 1 wei (the fee).
After a winning play, the pot is always zero and the bank balance increases by exactly 1 wei.
After a play(), if the player wins, the bank balance increases by exactly FEE_AMOUNT (1 wei) from before the call.
After a winning play() where random == 0, the caller's balance increases by pot minus FEE_AMOUNT before the transfer.

After a winning play() (random == 0), the caller's final balance equals msg.sender.balance before the call plus (pot + TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT) for the reference C, but equals msg.sender.balance before the call plus (pot + TICKET_AMOUNT) for the buggy version if the bank has enough funds.

After a play() call, the total contract balance (pot + contract's own ETH) equals the initial total plus TICKET_AMOUNT minus the fee (FEE_AMOUNT) that the bank receives in winning case, otherwise equals initial plus TICKET_AMOUNT.
